clusters.common_root: Effective write authority is reconstructed by separate callers instead of one intersection of Phase Policy, Intent, Classification, Blueprint, Role Policy, and Agent Assignment.
clusters.work_package: Implement computeEffectiveScope() and remove caller-local scope derivation.
clusters.reason: Scope authorization and proof provenance are both gate inputs, but one cannot substitute for the other.

clusters.common_root: Candidate Snapshot, STAGED_EXACT, scope validation, and preapproval are accepted as Task-authored labels and hashes rather than validator-issued, non-interchangeable proof types.
clusters.work_package: Define proof producers, proof-type discriminators, subject binding, file-set/hash verification, and consumer-side validation in validateTypedProof().
clusters.reason: A correctly typed proof can still be insufficient for execution approval unless the approval requirement is derived structurally.

clusters.common_root: Requirement IDs are not globally unique within the Task authority model, duplicate map entries overwrite one another, and waiver semantics are not resolved against exactly one required requirement.
clusters.work_package: Implement resolveUniqueRequirement(); reject duplicates before any Map projection; fail closed on waiver-like evidence until waiver support is either fully integrated or removed.
clusters.scope_decision: The identity invariant is mandatory. Phase 1 waiver capability should be removed unless its full authority and chronology contract is implemented in the same remediation.
clusters.reason: Both require unique resolution, but requirement semantics and artifact provenance have different schemas and consumers.

clusters.common_root: Cross-Task artifact and Domain approval lookups use first-match resolution, so a duplicate ID can redirect authority to an attacker-controlled artifact.
clusters.work_package: Implement resolveUniqueArtifact() for every manifest, evidence, approval, Rule, and Source reference; zero or multiple matches must fail closed.
clusters.deduplication: These two formal findings are different consumers of the same unsafe resolver root and form one deduplicated root cause.
clusters.reason: Unique lookup is necessary for Domain authority binding, but uniqueness alone does not prove the Rule/Approval/Source relationship.

clusters.common_root: Dedicated Domain schemas exist but the production schema loader does not load them, and the production validator performs only partial hand-written checks instead of one Rule/Approval/Source authority binding.
clusters.work_package: For the first commit, retain only proposed/unverified registry behavior and remove any claim that Phase 1 can confirm a Rule. Re-entry requires schema-loader integration and validateDomainApprovalBinding().
clusters.migration_320_effect: None toward execution: Migration 320 remains NO-GO because its Rule remains candidate/unverified.
clusters.alternative: IMPLEMENT is acceptable only if the complete three-party binding and production-path tests are delivered before A5.

clusters.common_root: Whether execution approval is required is inferred from free-text trigger regexes rather than structured Task effect categories.
clusters.work_package: Derive approval sensitivity from validated structured effect fields; free text may add sensitivity but must never remove it.
clusters.reason: This cluster decides that a proof is required; typed proof validation decides whether submitted proof is authoritative.

clusters.common_root: The 50-case suite encodes self-authored proof as a valid GO, while the 54-case suite predominantly tests isolated helpers and report shape instead of production integration and semantic outputs.
clusters.work_package: Replace fixture-count trust with production-path invariants, exact finding-class assertions, typed-proof provenance checks, resolver collision tests, and mutation resistance.
clusters.reason: Correct production enforcement and an oracle capable of detecting its removal are separate deliverables.

clusters.common_root: Scanner matching is applied to non-canonical representations, allowing JSON Unicode escapes to hide content declared detectable by policy.
clusters.work_package: Implement canonicalizeScannerInput() with bounded decoding and retain raw-to-canonical provenance in findings.
clusters.reason: The scanner findings share one pipeline architecture but enforce distinct declared classes and require separate invariants.

clusters.common_root: Credential/header parsing does not cover declared Basic authorization and quoted cookie representations after canonicalization.
clusters.work_package: Parse normalized header name/value pairs and emit stable classes for Basic credentials and sensitive quoted cookie values.

clusters.common_root: The policy implies opaque-token detection more broadly than the implemented entropy alphabet, so URL-safe tokens bypass the declared class.
clusters.work_package: For Phase 1, state the exact supported entropy alphabets and boundaries, remove broader claims, and fail closed for declared credential-bearing fields. Broader URL-safe entropy may be implemented later.
clusters.alternative: IMPLEMENT the URL-safe alphabet in the unified pipeline if false-positive bounds and tests can be specified before A5.

clusters.common_root: Policy declares an extension-versus-magic mismatch finding class that the scanner never emits.
clusters.work_package: Remove the unimplemented mismatch claim from Phase 1 while retaining the simpler fail-closed prohibition on unapproved binary artifacts.
clusters.reason: Binary prohibition is the enforceable Phase 1 control; an unused forensic claim adds false assurance without strengthening that gate.

clusters.common_root: Lifecycle state is projected from fixed A3/Remediation 4 sources and hard-coded booleans, so an active or completed A4 can still project a4_started=false.
clusters.work_package: Implement projectLifecycleState() over validated transition records and include the current review Task; reject missing, duplicate, contradictory, or regressive transitions.
clusters.reason: The present value is stale and misleading. It does not erase a filed BLOCKER because the gate is already NO-GO, but it must be fixed before lifecycle status can be authoritative.

A_scope_lattice.conclusion: The six authority layers are not passed through one common intersection function.

B_typed_proof_provenance.conclusion: Proof type, issuer, subject, file set, and digest are not jointly verified by the consuming production validator.

C_requirement_identity.conclusion: Duplicate IDs and waiver target resolution share a missing global uniqueness invariant.

D_artifact_authority_resolution.conclusion: Code and Domain findings share first-match artifact resolution; complete Domain binding remains an additional independent obligation.

E_scanner_pipeline.conclusion: There is no single raw-to-canonical-to-classification pipeline whose emitted classes are mechanically checked against policy; one declared class is not implemented at all.

F_domain_authority_application.conclusion: The dedicated schemas are absent from the production loader and the Rule/Approval/Source triple is not validated end to end.

G_lifecycle_projection.conclusion: The projection uses fixed known sources and hard-coded state, which excludes the current A4 lifecycle. This is an observed control gap, not an added formal A4 finding.

deduplication_summary.additional_gap: RC-A4-12-LIFECYCLE-PROJECTION is tracked separately and does not change the formal finding count.
